newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Vanadium prices to firm-Glencore S.Africa official.
newsitem.headline: Vanadium prices to firm-Glencore S.Africa official.

text.p: Vanadium prices are likely to firm in the future but major short-term price fluctuations as seen in the past are unlikely, Glencore International South Africa marketing director Les Ford said on Monday.
Speaking at a Metal Bulletin mining and metals conference, Ford said that with increasing demand for steel in the world, demand for vanadium was predicted to remain firm.
"With the tight supply and demand, vanadium prices are liable to firm to some extent in the future, but (will) not see some of the major short-term fluctuations shown in the past," Ford said.
He said a factor promoting price stability was the reduction in availability of Chinese vanadium on the world market, which promoted price stability.
"The increasing stability in the CIS makes disturbances in supply less likely from this area," he added.
But Ford predicted an increase in the recovery of vanadium -- used mostly in the steel industry -- from ashes and residues remaining after vanadium is extracted from oil-based materials.
He said in the past a proportion of these ashes and residues from catalysts were dumped but increasing environmental pressure had made dumping difficult and costly.
"Presently recovery of vanadium from ashes and residues accounts for 10 percent of world vanadium production.
"Vanadium recovery from these sources is predicted to rise to 20 percent of world vanadium production over the next 10 years," Ford said.
He added that South Africa, with about 42 percent of world vanadium reserves, would continue to play a major role in world production.
"With its natural resources and infrastructure, South Africa has some significant advantages over its competitors and will continue to be a low-cost producer".
